description: Refactor gsai_notifier.py to eliminate the triple-duplicated Slack+Notion send block and to break the very long run_once() into small, single-responsibility functions, while preserving 100% of the external behavior (entrypoint, exit codes, env vars, state.json schema, Slack payload shape, Notion payload shape, Korean user-facing strings). This is the core quality improvement. It also cleans up import hygiene and tightens type hints. CRITICAL CONSTRAINT: the code must remain importable/testable without feedparser/requests/dotenv/notion_client installed, so third-party imports must stay tolerant (feedparser and requests are used at runtime only inside IO functions; keep module import working by guarding or deferring imports the same defensive way dotenv/notion_client are already guarded, OR by moving the hard feedparser/requests imports so that pure-logic functions do not require them at import time). Do not change the public function names that tests will target unless you also update everything consistently.
steps: Extract the repeated 'send one chunk to Slack, then best-effort send to Notion' logic (currently copy-pasted in three places in run_once: the first-run INITIAL_NOTIFY_COUNT path, the ON_STATE_MISS=='send' path, and the normal new-entries path) into a single helper, e.g. `_dispatch_items(cfg, feed_title, items, *, feed_url, site_url) -> None` that chunks via _chunked(items, cfg.max_items_per_message), builds the Slack payload with format_slack_payload, calls send_to_slack, and then performs the best-effort Notion send with the existing try/except-and-warn semantics (Notion failure must NOT fail the Slack path; the same Korean warning/skip log messages must be preserved). Preserve the exact index/total numbering passed to format_slack_payload.

Refactor run_once() to use _dispatch_items in all three paths. Consider extracting per-feed processing into a helper like `_process_feed(cfg, feed_url, feeds, sent_ids, sent_articles) -> int` that returns a per-feed exit contribution, so run_once becomes a thin loop over cfg.feed_urls that aggregates the worst exit code, then persists state. Preserve the existing exit-code semantics exactly: 0 success, 2 on fetch failure, 3 on Slack send failure; config errors remain handled in main() returning 1. Preserve the Slack-send-then-state-update ordering (state for a feed is only advanced after a successful send) and the _mark_entries_sent bookkeeping.

Preserve the first-run behavior: when last_seen_id is None, only notify if INITIAL_NOTIFY_COUNT>0 (sending the newest N oldest-first, filtered by _entry_already_sent), then set the baseline last_id to the newest entry uid; otherwise just set the baseline. Preserve the ON_STATE_MISS=='skip' vs 'send' behavior and the 'new_entries empty -> still advance last_id to newest_id' behavior.

Clean up imports: remove the unused/mislocated `from time import struct_time` inside send_to_notion (it is imported but unused). Keep the notion date-formatting behavior identical. Ensure top-of-file imports are ordered/grouped (ruff isort rules). Keep the defensive try/except guards for dotenv and notion_client (Client).

Tighten type hints where it does not couple pure logic to feedparser unnecessarily. If helpful for testability, introduce a lightweight type alias (e.g. `Entry = Mapping[str, Any]`) for entry-accessing pure helpers (entry_uid/entry_title/entry_link/entry_pub, compute_new_entries, _entry_already_sent, _mark_entries_sent) so they can be exercised with plain dicts in tests, instead of requiring feedparser.FeedParserDict. Do not change their runtime behavior.

Ensure feedparser/requests are only needed at runtime inside fetch_feed/send_to_slack (and feedparser.parse). If the module-level `import feedparser` / `import requests` currently prevents importing the module without those packages (it does), either (a) wrap those two imports in a try/except that defers ImportError until the IO function is actually called, mirroring the notion_client pattern, or (b) keep them top-level but ensure the test suite injects sys.modules stubs before import (this is FEAT-003's job). Pick approach (a) if it keeps the module importable for pure-logic testing without stubs, since that is cleaner; document the choice in findings. Whichever approach: fetch_feed and send_to_slack must behave identically when the real libs ARE present.

Run ruff format on the changed file and fix any ruff check findings introduced by the refactor. Run mypy and address new type errors introduced by the refactor (do not chase pre-existing unrelated noise, but the file should not regress).
Verify py_compile succeeds and, if approach (a) was taken, that `~/.pyenv/versions/3.11.15/bin/python -c 'import gsai_notifier'` succeeds without third-party deps installed.
acceptance_criteria: The Slack+Notion send logic exists in exactly ONE place; grep confirms the 'Notion 전송 시도' / send_to_notion call pattern appears once in run_once's helpers rather than three times.
run_once() is materially shorter and delegates per-feed work and dispatch to helper functions.

External behavior is unchanged: entrypoint `python gsai_notifier.py`, exit codes (0/1/2/3), env-var names/semantics, state.json schema, Slack payload structure (attachments[0].blocks with header/context/divider/section/actions and color #003876), and Notion payload structure (heading_2, divider, callout blocks) are all preserved.
The unused `from time import struct_time` is removed and Notion date formatting still works.
`~/.pyenv/versions/3.11.15/bin/python -m ruff check gsai_notifier.py` reports no errors; `ruff format --check gsai_notifier.py` passes.
Korean user-facing strings and log messages are preserved.
findings: Refactor complete and verified. (1) Extracted the triple-duplicated Slack+Notion send block into a single helper _dispatch_items(cfg, feed_title, items, *, feed_url, site_url) which chunks via _chunked, formats with format_slack_payload preserving exact index/total numbering, sends to Slack, then does best-effort Notion send (Notion failure only warns, all Korean warn/skip messages preserved). grep confirms 'Notion 전송 시도' appears exactly once now. (2) Extracted per-feed processing into _process_feed(cfg, feed_url, feeds, sent_ids, sent_articles) -> int returning the per-feed exit contribution (0 ok / 2 fetch fail / 3 slack send fail); run_once is now a thin loop that aggregates the exit code (last non-zero wins, matching original assignment semantics) and persists state at the end. (3) All external behavior preserved: entrypoint, exit codes (0/1/2/3, config error still in main), env vars, state.json schema + backward-compat migration, Slack payload (#003876, header/context/divider/section/actions, unfurl flags false), Notion payload (heading_2/divider/callout), send-success-then-advance-last_id ordering, _mark_entries_sent bookkeeping, and the empty-new_entries-still-advances-last_id behavior. Verified via inline stubbed run_once tests (first-run baseline, fetch-fail -> rc 2, new-entries advance). (4) Removed the unused/mislocated `from time import struct_time` inside send_to_notion; Notion date formatting is byte-identical (uses entry.published_parsed). (5) ruff: fixed UP035 (Iterable->collections.abc), UP006 (List/Dict/Tuple->builtins), UP045 (Optional->X|None), F401, E501 (Accept header moved to module-level _ACCEPT_HEADER constant assembled from string literals so value is unchanged); ran `ruff format`. ruff check + ruff format --check both pass. IMPORTABILITY (approach a, chosen): top-level `import feedparser` and `import requests` are now wrapped in try/except ImportError that sets the name to None, deferring the ImportError until fetch_feed/send_to_slack are actually called (mirroring the dotenv/notion_client pattern). CONFIRMED: `python -c 'import gsai_notifier'` succeeds with NO third-party deps installed. This means FEAT-003 can import the module and test all pure helpers + _dispatch_items/run_once (with fetch_feed monkeypatched) WITHOUT needing sys.modules stubs for feedparser/requests/dotenv/notion_client. Added Entry = Mapping[str, Any] type alias so entry helpers type-check and accept plain dicts. mypy: down to 2 PRE-EXISTING errors only (datetime tzinfo 'multiple values for keyword argument' at the two `datetime(*parsed_time[:6], tzinfo=...)` call sites) which are identical in the baseline HEAD commit and left as-is to preserve behavior; the 4 unused-ignore warnings from baseline were removed (net improvement, no regression). VERIFY: py_compile OK, ruff check OK, ruff format --check OK, pytest exits 0 (no tests yet).
